currentContext.strengths: Backed by BASF SE, the ultimate holding company (52.75% direct + 20.58% via BASF Schweiz AG), providing technology, brand and global scale.|Diversified portfolio across six business segments (Agricultural Solutions, Industrial Solutions, Materials, Surface Technologies, Nutrition & Care, Chemicals) reduces reliance on any single end-market.|Broad customer base of 5,000+ spanning large global companies, SMEs and end-users (e.g. farmers) across both B2B and B2C channels.|'Local-for-local' manufacturing strategy underway (Cellasto plant at Dahej, dispersions capacity expansion at Mangalore) to serve growing Indian demand domestically.|CRISIL AAA/Stable long-term credit rating (reaffirmed during the year) alongside nil borrowings at FY26 year-end.
currentContext.strategies: 'Local-for-local' manufacturing strategy — expanding India-based capacity (Cellasto plant at Dahej, dispersions capacity expansion at Mangalore) to support sustainable growth and enhanced customer engagement.|Differentiated steering of businesses: demerging the Agricultural Solutions business into a separately listed entity (BASF Agricultural Solutions India Ltd) to allow it greater agility and sharper focus while remaining aligned with BASF's global strategy.|Sustainability transition across manufacturing sites — advancing initiatives to reduce Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, including procuring renewable energy via a hybrid solar and wind project (Clean Max) for Gujarat sites.|Portfolio strengthening through new product introductions in high-growth segments such as insecticides, biostimulants and specialty applications (e.g. Valexio®, Mibelya®), and circular/sustainable solutions (Tinuvin® NOR® platform).|Operational excellence focus: working capital efficiency, optimal asset utilization and disciplined cost management.|Safety-first culture with a stated goal of zero incidents and continuous improvement of leading safety indicators.
currentContext.expansion: The Company continued to expand its manufacturing footprint and strengthen innovation capability in India under a 'local-for-local' strategy. The Cellasto® plant at Dahej (automotive NVH reduction solutions) has a capacity enhancement project well on track to meet growing automotive industry demand. Dispersions capacity at the Mangalore site is being expanded to support future growth and meet increasing customer demand across coatings, construction chemicals and related industries. During the year, a dispersion plant debottlenecking project at the Dahej site enhanced plant capacity by around 10%. Ultramid® polyamide grade production capacity was increased at both the Panoli and Thane sites to meet growing market demand. Separately, in the Surface Technologies segment, BASF and Carlyle reached a binding transaction agreement in October 2025 to create a leading standalone global coatings company; as part of this, the Company has decided to transfer its 100% shareholding in BASF India Coatings Private Limited (its wholly owned subsidiary housing the Automotive Coatings & Refinish business) to Carlyle companies, with the transaction expected to conclude by Q2 2026, subject to approvals. The Company's Chemical Catalysts business also launched X3D®, described as the world's first 3D printed catalyst, positioned to lower capex for new projects and debottleneck existing assets with better productivity and energy efficiency. Digital transformation initiatives across sites include a digital energy monitoring system (EMS) at Dahej, digitalised work permits, a digitized shopfloor checklist at Thane, and an automated energy management dashboard at Panoli.
currentContext.mdna: Global macroeconomic environment shaped by geopolitical uncertainties, supply chain disruptions and volatility in energy and feedstock markets placed sustained pressure on industrial value chains, along with pricing challenges across the chemical industry impacting margins and business sentiment.|India's economic fundamentals remained robust, supported by stable domestic consumption, continued policy momentum and sustained industrial growth, providing a supportive demand backdrop despite global headwinds.|Revenue growth was modest but supported by volume growth in key segments, with particularly strong performance in the Nutrition & Care and Industrial Solutions segments despite softer market conditions.|Profitability was impacted by higher input costs and prevailing market challenges, partly offset by disciplined cost management, portfolio optimization and operational excellence.

risks.risk: Material dependence on related-party (intra-group) trading transactions with fellow BASF SE subsidiaries.
risks.note: BASF Hong Kong Ltd and BASF South East Asia Pte Ltd — both subsidiaries of the same ultimate holding company, BASF SE, Germany, engaged in trading of chemicals and chemical products with BASF India — are proposed related-party counterparties for FY2026-27 whose transactions are expected to exceed the amended SEBI materiality threshold (10% of consolidated turnover, i.e. Rs. 1,494 crore, based on FY26 consolidated turnover of Rs. 14,944 crore), requiring member approval under Regulation 23 of the SEBI Listing Regulations. This signals a structurally significant reliance on intra-group trading relationships rather than fully independent third-party commercial dealings.

one-line thesis: BASF India is demerging its agricultural solutions business into a separately listed pure-play entity, **BASF Agricultural Solutions India Limited (BASIL)**, on a **1:1 share-entitlement** basis (one BASIL share per BASF India share held). SEBI and both exchanges have already issued no-objection letters; management guides an **18–20 month** approval process with BASIL listing / share allotment expected **Jan–Mar 2027**. The ag business posted **sales of ₹1,944 cr and PBT of ₹254 cr in FY25-26**, with 12 products launched since 2022 now ~25% of India sales — the demerger is pitched as a focus/value-unlock event, not a capital raise or dilution.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Period | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Agri-solutions sales | ₹1,944 cr | n/d | FY25-26 (full year), agri segment only — the business being demerged |
| Agri-solutions PBT | ₹254 cr | n/d | FY25-26; ~13% PBT margin |
| New-product contribution | ~25% of India sales | — | 12 new products launched since 2022 ("continuous innovation engine") |
| Revenue / EBITDA / order book / net debt | — | — | Not disclosed — this is an NCLT scheme meeting, not results |
> No quarterly P&L was presented. Figures above are FY25-26 annual for the ag business only; BASF India's remaining (chemicals) business financials were not broken out on this call.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Demerger scheme approval:** ~**18–20 months** all-in for the scheme to clear multiple regulators (Stock Exchanges, SEBI, NCLT, RoC, Regional Directorate).
- **BASIL listing / allotment:** allotment of BASIL shares expected **completed by March 2027**; listing on **BSE & NSE**, ideally **Jan–Mar 2027** (subject to requisite approvals).
- **Share entitlement ratio:** **1:1** — one BASIL share for every BASF India share held (all shareholders, promoter + non-promoter, as on a record date to be fixed).
- **Approvals already in hand:** no-objection letters received from **SEBI and both Stock Exchanges**; final court hearing pending.
- **Dividend policy (post-demerger):** asked by a shareholder — **not answered / not yet decided** on the call.
- No revenue-growth or margin guidance given (not an earnings call).
order book & pipeline: Not applicable / not disclosed (NCLT scheme meeting).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- The demerger carves out the **agricultural solutions business** (seeds, seed-treatment, crop protection — fungicides/herbicides/insecticides/biologicals, plus digital farming) into **BASIL**, leaving BASF India with the **remaining chemicals businesses** ("seven segments" of chemistry, per a shareholder's paraphrase).
- Post-demerger, BASIL will be housed as a stand-alone entity with **its own management, MD, CFO, company secretary, independent directors and Board** — the specific board/management is **not yet decided** (to be finalized closer to implementation).
- Own **ERP system** to be implemented for the agrochemical entity to sharpen speed/transparency/decision-making.
growth verticals / optionality:
- Innovation engine: **12 new products since 2022 = ~25% of India sales**; portfolio spans seeds, seed-treatment, crop protection and **digital farming solutions**.
- India positioning: "one of the largest shares of global arable land" → headroom for productivity gains; BASF frames itself as an integrated agrochemical solutions provider capturing India's agri-growth opportunity.
- Post-demerger the pure-play structure is meant to enable faster response to agri cycles via **industry-tailored KPIs** and a more agile structure while retaining strategic linkage to BASF global.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Only datapoint: ag-business **PBT margin ~13%** (₹254 cr on ₹1,944 cr, FY25-26).
- **Demerger cost:** most work done **in-house** (legal, finance, tax, HR, business units); external agencies used only for share-entitlement ratio, fairness opinion, and NCLT representation → cost kept low (specific stamp-duty / legal / valuation amount **not quantified** despite a shareholder asking).
capex / expansion (watch slippage): No capex or capacity plans disclosed. The only "expansion" is corporate/structural (the demerger + a new ERP for BASIL). Key date to watch for slippage: **BASIL listing Jan–Mar 2027** (management's own 18–20 month timeline flagged NCLT/regulatory delays as the risk).
capital allocation:
- Demerger via **1:1 share entitlement** — no cash outflow to shareholders, no dilution; existing holders become direct owners of BASIL.
- Rationale cited: "better capital allocation in accordance with the focused strategic orientation" of each business; stronger investment/risk profile as a pure-play.
- Post-demerger dividend policy for both entities **not yet articulated**.
risks & watch-items:
- **Regulatory/timeline risk:** 18–20 month multi-regulator approval; NCLT delays explicitly acknowledged (a shareholder noted "too delayed in our country, NCLT").
- **Minority-shareholder concern (dissent):** one shareholder (Ankur Chanda) challenged the process — alleged inadequate transparency, limited disclosure, and that the transaction may "primarily benefit promoters/controlling stakeholder" rather than minorities, and asked what accountability management takes if value erosion follows. Management's blanket answer: 1:1 ratio for all shareholders → "no detrimental impact."
- **Open items:** BASIL board/management not yet named; dividend policy undecided.
- Standard scheme conditionality: resolution "deemed passed subject to receipt of requisite number of votes" via remote e-voting.
management quality / tone:
- MD Alexander Gerding's remarks were strategic and farmer/innovation-themed ("for the love of farming, the biggest job on Earth"; Suraksha Hamesha safety training reaching ~60m farmers over a decade).
- Tone from the vast majority of retail shareholders was warmly supportive — many praised CS Manohar Kamath and the secretarial team ("Vidya ji") and treated the 1:1 BASIL entitlement as a "bonus." Only one shareholder registered substantive dissent on governance/valuation.
- Management answered cost/timeline/benefit/board questions directly but left **dividend policy and the specific demerger cost quantum unanswered**.
non-obvious takeaways:
- This is a **value-unlock corporate action to watch, not an operating quarter** — the investable event is the BASIL listing (Jan–Mar 2027) and the eventual separate trading of a **pure-play Indian agrochemicals** company (₹1,944 cr sales, ~13% PBT margin, 25% new-product mix).
- Management hinted at **more portfolio surgery ahead** — a shareholder said he looks forward to further "merger and sale of parts of BASF"; management's framing (industry-tailored KPIs, own ERP, agility) is consistent with a broader restructuring of the Indian entity.
- The remaining BASF India (post-demerger) becomes a cleaner **specialty-chemicals** play once the ag business exits — relevant for how the stub re-rates.
- Retail-heavy register with high goodwill = low deal-block risk at the meeting; the lone governance objection is the only friction point on record.

themes.title: Agrochemicals & crop-input cycle recovery
themes.need: Crop-protection is recovering off a brutal trough, and Q1FY27 shows domestic branded volume decoupling from generic exports. RALLIS grew revenue only 7% yet lifted EBITDA 23% to a ~18.0% margin (+230bps) as domestic B2C rose 19% on +15% volume while exports COLLAPSED 28% (volume -35%) on Chinese pricing, and its seeds EBITDA margin went 26% to 30% on a rice/maize/millet mix versus price-controlled cotton - though PAT +31% is flattered by an INR 35cr employee-provision reversal of which INR 24cr is genuinely one-time, so normalise before extrapolating. The monsoon is the live variable: as of 8-Jul seasonal rainfall was ~15% below normal with kharif acreage ~21% below last year. SUMICHEM delivered record FY26 profitability; INSECTICID/DHANUKA/SHARDACROP ride premiumization + technicals; COROMANDEL/GNFC/CHAMBLFERT/GODREJAGRO add fertilizers + integrated agri.
themes.driver: Monsoon catch-up and kharif acreage recovery from ~21% below last year; domestic B2C volume against continued Chinese export price pressure; new molecule launches and biologicals scale-up.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: BASF India manufactures and trades chemicals and chemical products (100% of turnover) organised into six business segments — Agricultural Solutions; Industrial Solutions (Dispersions & Performance Chemicals); Materials (Performance Materials & Monomers); Surface Technologies (Coatings, via wholly-owned subsidiary BASF India Coatings Private Limited); Nutrition & Care (Care Chemicals & Nutrition & Health); and Chemicals (Intermediates & Petrochemicals). group_structure.body:

- BASF Catalysts India Private Limited — related party: Affiliate company of BASF India Limited; the Company placed Inter-Corporate Deposits with it during FY26.
- BASF Chemicals India Private Limited — related party: Affiliate company of BASF India Limited; the Company placed Inter-Corporate Deposits with it during FY26.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global macroeconomic environment shaped by geopolitical uncertainties, supply chain disruptions and volatility in energy and feedstock markets placed sustained pressure on industrial value chains, along with pricing challenges across the chemical industry impacting margins and business sentiment.
- India's economic fundamentals remained robust, supported by stable domestic consumption, continued policy momentum and sustained industrial growth, providing a supportive demand backdrop despite global headwinds.
- Revenue growth was modest but supported by volume growth in key segments, with particularly strong performance in the Nutrition & Care and Industrial Solutions segments despite softer market conditions.
- Profitability was impacted by higher input costs and prevailing market challenges, partly offset by disciplined cost management, portfolio optimization and operational excellence.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- Only datapoint: ag-business **PBT margin ~13%** (₹254 cr on ₹1,944 cr, FY25-26).
- **Demerger cost:** most work done **in-house** (legal, finance, tax, HR, business units); external agencies used only for share-entitlement ratio, fairness opinion, and NCLT representation → cost kept low (specific stamp-duty / legal / valuation amount **not quantified** despite a shareholder asking).

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Demerger via **1:1 share entitlement** — no cash outflow to shareholders, no dilution; existing holders become direct owners of BASIL.
- Rationale cited: "better capital allocation in accordance with the focused strategic orientation" of each business; stronger investment/risk profile as a pure-play.
- Post-demerger dividend policy for both entities **not yet articulated**.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company continued to expand its manufacturing footprint and strengthen innovation capability in India under a 'local-for-local' strategy. The Cellasto® plant at Dahej (automotive NVH reduction solutions) has a capacity enhancement project well on track to meet growing automotive industry demand. Dispersions capacity at the Mangalore site is being expanded to support future growth and meet increasing customer demand across coatings, construction chemicals and related industries. During the year, a dispersion plant debottlenecking project at the Dahej site enhanced plant capacity by around 10%. Ultramid® polyamide grade production capacity was increased at both the Panoli and Thane sites to meet growing market demand. Separately, in the Surface Technologies segment, BASF and Carlyle reached a binding transaction agreement in October 2025 to create a leading standalone global coatings company; as part of this, the Company has decided to transfer its 100% shareholding in BASF India Coatings Private Limited (its wholly owned subsidiary housing the Automotive Coatings & Refinish business) to Carlyle companies, with the transaction expected to conclude by Q2 2026, subject to approvals. The Company's Chemical Catalysts business also launched X3D®, described as the world's first 3D printed catalyst, positioned to lower capex for new projects and debottleneck existing assets with better productivity and energy efficiency. Digital transformation initiatives across sites include a digital energy monitoring system (EMS) at Dahej, digitalised work permits, a digitized shopfloor checklist at Thane, and an automated energy management dashboard at Panoli.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body:
- MD Alexander Gerding's remarks were strategic and farmer/innovation-themed ("for the love of farming, the biggest job on Earth"; Suraksha Hamesha safety training reaching ~60m farmers over a decade).
- Tone from the vast majority of retail shareholders was warmly supportive — many praised CS Manohar Kamath and the secretarial team ("Vidya ji") and treated the 1:1 BASIL entitlement as a "bonus." Only one shareholder registered substantive dissent on governance/valuation.
- Management answered cost/timeline/benefit/board questions directly but left **dividend policy and the specific demerger cost quantum unanswered**.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Backed by BASF SE, the ultimate holding company (52.75% direct + 20.58% via BASF Schweiz AG), providing technology, brand and global scale.
- Diversified portfolio across six business segments (Agricultural Solutions, Industrial Solutions, Materials, Surface Technologies, Nutrition & Care, Chemicals) reduces reliance on any single end-market.
- Broad customer base of 5,000+ spanning large global companies, SMEs and end-users (e.g. farmers) across both B2B and B2C channels.
- 'Local-for-local' manufacturing strategy underway (Cellasto plant at Dahej, dispersions capacity expansion at Mangalore) to serve growing Indian demand domestically.
- CRISIL AAA/Stable long-term credit rating (reaffirmed during the year) alongside nil borrowings at FY26 year-end.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Regulatory/timeline risk:** 18–20 month multi-regulator approval; NCLT delays explicitly acknowledged (a shareholder noted "too delayed in our country, NCLT").
- **Minority-shareholder concern (dissent):** one shareholder (Ankur Chanda) challenged the process — alleged inadequate transparency, limited disclosure, and that the transaction may "primarily benefit promoters/controlling stakeholder" rather than minorities, and asked what accountability management takes if value erosion follows. Management's blanket answer: 1:1 ratio for all shareholders → "no detrimental impact."
- **Open items:** BASIL board/management not yet named; dividend policy undecided.
- Standard scheme conditionality: resolution "deemed passed subject to receipt of requisite number of votes" via remote e-voting.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- This is a **value-unlock corporate action to watch, not an operating quarter** — the investable event is the BASIL listing (Jan–Mar 2027) and the eventual separate trading of a **pure-play Indian agrochemicals** company (₹1,944 cr sales, ~13% PBT margin, 25% new-product mix).
- Management hinted at **more portfolio surgery ahead** — a shareholder said he looks forward to further "merger and sale of parts of BASF"; management's framing (industry-tailored KPIs, own ERP, agility) is consistent with a broader restructuring of the Indian entity.
- The remaining BASF India (post-demerger) becomes a cleaner **specialty-chemicals** play once the ag business exits — relevant for how the stub re-rates.
- Retail-heavy register with high goodwill = low deal-block risk at the meeting; the lone governance objection is the only friction point on record.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demerger] The Agricultural Solutions business is being demerged from BASF India Ltd into a separately listed entity, BASF Agricultural Solutions India Limited (BASIL): cleared by SEBI and stock exchanges on 2 Feb 2026 (No-Objection Letters), applications filed with the NCLT on 16 Feb 2026, favourable NCLT orders on 8 Apr 2026 dispensing the creditors meeting and directing a shareholders meeting, shareholders meeting fixed for 24 June 2026 (voting 19-23 June 2026), share entitlement ratio 1:1, and completion expected during FY 26-27.
- [Divestment] Coatings: the Automotive OEM and Automotive Refinish Coatings business has been carried out under BASF India Coatings Pvt Ltd (a wholly owned subsidiary) since 1 January 2025; as of 31 March 2026 it generated sales of Rs. 595 crore, representing 4% of consolidated sales; the India valuation is Rs. 230.16 crore based on an independent valuation; globally BASF will reinvest holding a 40% equity stake in the new Global Coatings Standalone Company under Carlyle; the transaction is expected to close by Q2 of calendar year 2026 subject to regulatory approvals, after which BASF India Coatings Pvt Ltd ceases to be a wholly owned subsidiary.
- [Macro] Macro-economic context until March 2026: West Asia crisis impact including feedstock inflation from a surge in oil and gas prices, route disruptions driving up ocean freight (Strait of Hormuz) and INR depreciation, against low inflation, easing interest rates and GST rationalisation supporting consumption; a prolonged crisis is flagged as potentially a drag on growth.
- [Agri macro] The West Asia conflict is described as affecting Indian agriculture through disrupted Gulf supplies (urea, DAP, LNG, sulphur) raising prices and subsidy pressure ahead of Kharif, pressure on crop protection product cost and availability, pressure on farm profitability, and export disruption for rice, grapes, pomegranate, onion, chilli and cumin.
- [Reporting basis] Financial disclosures in the deck are consolidated and include discontinued operations (the Coatings business); discontinued operations are separately noted as Jan to Mar 26 revenue 162 and PBTbEI 6, and Apr to Mar 26 revenue 595 and PBTbEI 3.
